summary.headline: Karamtara Q1 FY27 revenue rose 72% YoY to Rs 1,581 crore, with EBITDA margin at about 11% held back by freight and fuel costs.
summary.overview: Karamtara Engineering, listed recently, reported Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of Rs 1,581 crore (up 72% YoY), with renewable products at 82% of revenue. EBITDA was Rs 174 crore (up 45% YoY) and PAT Rs 87 crore (up 45% YoY), with EBITDA margin about 11%. Management said elevated shipping, trucking and fuel costs compressed margins, which it expects to ease as utilisation rises and new contracts pass on these costs. Management reiterated an internal growth target of about 60-65% for FY27 and declined to guide FY28 numbers.

financial_highlights.change: Q1 FY26 was about 13% per management
down from 43 days in prior quarter and 67 days a year earlier
vs Rs 113 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Structures for fixed tilt and tracker plants, including mounting structures, tracker piles and stamp parts. Management cited solar revenue of about Rs 5,500 crore for the year, up from about Rs 20 crore in FY21.

segments.name: Wind
segments.commentary: Tubular and hybrid lattice towers. Hybrid towers can be switched to transmission towers, so wind capacity is fungible with transmission.

segments.name: Transmission
segments.commentary: Lattice towers up to 1200 kV plus hardware (insulator fittings, clamps, dampers). Management called it a key growth driver; the Bachao facility began manufacturing recently and is reaching peak in 6-9 months.

segments.name: Fasteners
segments.commentary: Bolts, nuts, studs and washers for solar, wind, transmission, bridges and railways.

segments.name: PEB (new)
segments.commentary: Pre-engineered buildings for data centres, a new business line with a Bachao facility coming up. Margin expected to be at least in line with other businesses; no numeric target given.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth target of about 60-65% YoY, which management said it hopes to achieve; no FY28 guidance given.
Revenue split of about 40-42% in H1 and 58-60% in H2, based on the company's historical pattern.
Margins expected to improve as utilisation rises in Q3 and Q4, but no numeric margin guidance was given.
Saudi Arabia facility: trials around December, commercial production around end-2026 or early 2027, with 12-18 months to reach target utilisation.
Bachao (India) facility: peak capacity expected in 6-9 months.
PEB facility: expected to start by the beginning of next financial year.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity 889,200 metric tonnes per annum, excluding rolling and galvanising capacity used captively.
13 manufacturing facilities: 8 in Maharashtra (7 Boisar, 1 Nagpur), 4 in Gujarat (Bachao) and 1 in Iqli.
FY26 capex about Rs 900 crore; capex continuing in FY27.
Under construction: new rolling mill and PEB facility at Bachao; solar stamp parts facility at Boisar; multi-product facility in Saudi Arabia for transmission and solar products.
Saudi galvanising plant expected online by February or March 2027.
demand_pricing: Management says demand continues to outpace supply and it is selective on orders to protect commercial terms.
US: Section 232 steel and aluminium tariff at 50%; management said the tariff was passed through to buyers, and reported tariff-linked revenue was Rs 250 crore in Q1 FY27.
US domestic steel supply is short; lead times of 6-8 months; local US prices about 30-40% above Indian import prices, per management.
Domestic solar contracts run 4-5 months with steel and zinc covered by pre-booking; export contracts run 8-9 months with imported raw material; price variation clauses on longer contracts.
Freight and fuel costs rose globally and hit margins in Q1, per management.
Exports to more than 50 countries; management cited Saudi Arabia's renewable and transmission plans as a demand driver.

qa_highlights.question: Business mix and transmission strategy; what is the supply-demand outlook for transmission towers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said transmission will be a key growth driver, given its history as a tower maker, the new Bachao capacity, and Saudi investment. It plans to build a large transmission portfolio in the way it built solar.

qa_highlights.question: Q2 trend and margin trajectory?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is going well and the company targets 60-65% growth. Margin was 11% in Q1 and is expected to improve as revenue and asset utilisation rise.

qa_highlights.question: How are contracts structured (cost-plus, fixed price, or both)?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic solar contracts are 4-5 months with steel and zinc pre-booked; export contracts are 8-9 months with imported raw material. Price variation clauses apply to longer contracts, and some large overseas transmission contracts are FOB with shipping passed through.

qa_highlights.question: US tariff exposure and cost competitiveness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 50% Section 232 tariff is fixed and stacking tariffs do not apply, and the tariff was fully passed to buyers. No major Indian competitor was seen in these products in the US.

qa_highlights.question: Why is margin not higher and what drives expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said shipping and trucking costs are at record highs, which has cut margins. Operating leverage from ramp-up of new capacity with fixed costs already in place should lift margins, and local-content plants such as Saudi Arabia should earn better margins.

qa_highlights.question: Capacity utilisation: can it exceed 75%, given a historical 55-60% range?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY26 utilisation was low because facilities came online late in the year. Utilisation is rising with the ramp-up, and new capacity takes 12-18 months to mature. No utilisation target was stated.

qa_highlights.question: Capital allocation beyond solar and transmission, and the PEB entry?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said capital goes to fungible, high-margin businesses. It shut a Nagpur rolling mill and moved passenger capacity there. PEB for data centres is a natural fit with existing clients and is expected to earn margins similar to other businesses (11-13% was not confirmed).

qa_highlights.question: Working capital and cash conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Working capital cycle fell from 67 to 43 days and then to 36 days. Interest cost is 2.6% of revenue, and management expects it to fall once IPO proceeds are deployed. FY26 EBITDA was about Rs 500 crore against cash conversion of about Rs 675 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff-linked revenue, Q1 FY27 vs Q1 FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Tariff-linked revenue was about Rs 250 crore in Q1 FY27, against Rs 113 crore in Q1 FY26 and about Rs 196 crore in the previous quarter. Costs of tariffs and freight are passed through to customers, so profitability is not affected.

risks_watch: Freight, fuel and trucking costs remain elevated; management said margins are held back until these ease or new contracts pass them through.
Ramp-up risk at Saudi Arabia (commercial production expected around year-end 2026 or early 2027), with 12-18 months to reach target utilisation.
US tariff exposure: 50% Section 232 tariff, with buyers bearing the cost; any change in US policy is a watch item.
Utilisation: historically 55-60%, and management did not state the level needed to meet the 60-65% growth target.
Other expenses were about Rs 500 crore in Q1 and include tariff and freight costs. Management gave no split.
Geopolitical conflict in the Middle East was mentioned as a possible factor for the Saudi project, though management said demand remains strong.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, growth and the transmission and Saudi pipeline. Cautious and non-committal on specific margin and FY28 numbers, and on whether the 11% margin is sustainable.
key_quotes: So yes, transmission is going to be a very, very large growth driver for us.
Our large installed capacity gives us flexibility to accept orders, which is the parameters that align with our strategic objectives while maintaining discipline on commercial terms.
We are predominantly a product company and you know we'd like to stay that way that's the character of the company that we are building.

adds.what: Saudi Arabia multi-product facility (transmission and solar products), trials ~Dec 2026, commercial production end-2026 or early 2027
Bachao (India) facility, peak capacity in 6-9 months; transmission manufacturing started recently
PEB facility at Bachao for data centres, expected to start by beginning of next financial year
Solar stamp parts facility at Boisar

growth.why: Management 'endeavours' to grow revenue 60-65% in FY27 (held), backed by Saudi and Bachao capacity coming live over the next 2-3 quarters, tariff pass-through revenue of Rs 250 cr, and demand exceeding supply; backing is partial since no quantified capacity additions or order book figures were given for the growth target.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 EBITDA margin about 11% vs about 13% in Q1 FY26, held back by shipping, trucking and fuel costs; management expects improvement as utilisation rises in Q3-Q4 and new contracts pass costs through, but gave no numeric margin guidance.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Bachao transmission facility already manufacturing (peak in 6-9 months), Saudi multi-product plant in trials around Dec 2026 with commercial production end-2026 or early 2027, and PEB facility expected by start of next financial year; capex of about Rs 900 crore in FY26 continues in FY27.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets 60-65% FY27 revenue growth with 58-60% of revenue expected in H2 per historical pattern; Q1 sales volume about 135,000 tonnes and demand is outpacing supply, though no quantified volume target was given.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation has historically been 55-60% and was low in FY26, so it is not at 80%+; however capex is being raised with rolling mill, PEB, stamp parts and Saudi facilities already under construction, and management continues to invest, making a further capex announcement plausible but not firmly guided.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only said it 'endeavours' to achieve 60-65% FY27 growth, declined FY28 guidance and was non-committal on margin, so no clear basis for raising guidance was shown.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Freight and fuel costs at record highs held margin to about 11% vs 13%, Saudi ramp-up takes 12-18 months to reach target utilisation, and Middle East conflict was flagged as a possible factor for the Saudi project.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: PEB (pre-engineered buildings) for data centres is a new business line with its Bachao facility expected to start by the beginning of next financial year, and Saudi multi-product facility starts commercial production around end-2026 or early 2027.

rows.label: Saudi Arabia facility commercial production
rows.why: Trials around Dec 2026 with commercial production around end-2026 or early 2027, followed by 12-18 months to reach target utilisation; galvanising plant online Feb-Mar 2027.

rows.label: Tariff pass-through revenue
rows.why: Tariff-linked revenue of Rs 250 crore in Q1 FY27 vs Rs 113 crore in Q1 FY26 and Rs 196 crore in the prior quarter, with 50% Section 232 tariff fixed and passed to buyers; tariff and freight costs passed through so profitability not affected.

rows.label: Working capital cycle reduction
rows.why: Working capital cycle fell from 67 to 43 to 36 days, and management expects interest cost (2.6% of revenue) to fall once IPO proceeds are deployed.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, the 60-65% FY27 growth aim, transmission and the Saudi pipeline, but cautious and non-committal on margin sustainability and FY28 numbers; analysts probed margin drivers (freight costs), utilisation levels versus the 55-60% historical range, and capital allocation
